subject.title: Design: Telegram isolated ingress holds per-chat lane for the entire agent turn — long turns block the group, then die at 25 min

question: Should Telegram isolated ingress release the per-chat/topic spool lane at durable dispatch handoff instead of holding it for the full agent turn, and what contract should own replay, ordering, and timeout recovery after that handoff?
rationale: The source problem is clear, but the fix crosses Telegram spool durability, reply-fence supersede behavior, same-lane ordering, session admission, and backend steering semantics, so automation should not choose the permanent contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Detach At Durable Handoff
options.body: Complete the spool claim once the inbound has been durably recorded or admitted to session machinery, then shrink the timeout guard to dispatch/handoff and prove replay safety.

options.title: Keep Transport-Lane Ownership
options.body: Preserve current full-turn lane ownership and focus only on progress, timeout messaging, or operator visibility, accepting that same-lane steering remains blocked during long turns.

options.title: Fold Into Run-Lifecycle Stack
options.body: Wait for the broader run-lifecycle work to settle a shared queue/admission invariant before changing Telegram's transport drain ownership.

recommendation.title: Detach At Durable Handoff
recommendation.body: Complete the spool claim once the inbound has been durably recorded or admitted to session machinery, then shrink the timeout guard to dispatch/handoff and prove replay safety.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the current design issue, authored the linked run-lifecycle integration stack, and are the live assignee for the production incident follow-up.
